title: Observability priority lens — instrumentation & span patterns
content:
Purpose:
Short notes to align the next sprint of telemetry work with product priorities. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — prioritization and small, testable changes. Focus areas: latency attribution (token path), cache-warmth signal, and tracing anchors that make root-cause visible with a 3-minute investigation flow.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Investigations for an observed latency spike should hit a small set of panels + 1 trace example within 3 minutes.
- Reduce noisy/low-signal metrics by 40% (trim away panels that don’t aid triage).
- Add lightweight span metadata to cover routing & fallback decisions (so operator can see which fallback executed and why).

Stakeholders / consumers:
- Oncall SREs: quick triage signals and examples for runbooks.
- Serving runtime engineers: kernel selection & cache patterns.
- Product/Console owners: per-route dashboards and alerting posture.

Priority metric definitions (compact, consistent naming conventions):
1) inference.request.count
   - Type: counter (increment on request start)
   - Labels: model, route, tier, region, customer_tier
   - Use: baseline throughput, anomaly detection (delta over 1m/5m)

2) inference.latency.first_token_ms
   - Type: histogram/summary (bucketed ms)
   - Labels: model, route, region, kv_warmth (hot|warm|cold), fallback_reason (none|rate_limit|capacity)
   - Recommended buckets: [1,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2000]
   - SLO use: p50/p90/p95/p99 pinned per model+route

3) inference.latency.token_tail_ms
   - Type: histogram (for tail behavior across entire token path)
   - Labels: same as first_token. Helpful to show long tail due to KV cache eviction or slow kernels.

4) kvcache.hit_ratio
   - Type: gauge (moving window)
   - Labels: model, shard, region, tenant_weight
   - Note: compute on the write-side aggregator with consistent TTL to avoid flapping.

5) fallback.invocations_total
   - Type: counter
   - Labels: fallback_type (model_variant|region|tier_fallback), route, cause (OOM|TIMEOUT|CAPACITY)
   - Use: actionable alarm when > X/min for a route (indicates degraded stack)

6) inference.tokens.generated
   - Type: counter
   - Labels: model, route, generation_mode (streaming|batch), region

7) trace.sampled_ratio_by_route
   - Type: gauge
   - Labels: route, model, sampling_policy
   - Use: ensure we keep sampling on low-traffic routes for problem reproducibility

Tracing conventions (span naming, minimal payload, and quick-decoding semantics):
- Span name pattern: <service>.<operation>[:detail]
  - Examples: runtime.generate:init, kv.cache_lookup, router.route_decision:fallback
- Top-level trace attributes (tags): request_id, route, model, customer_tier, kv_warmth, fallback_applied (true|false), kernel_name
- Span annotations: token_index (for long-running spans that process tokens), batch_id (if batched), seq_len_estimate
- Prefer structured attribute keys (snake_case) to allow fast filtering in trace UI.
- Sampling decisions: reservoir sampling with low-rate deterministic sampling for high-volume routes (e.g., 0.1% for popular routes) plus rate-limited error-based sampling for all routes (on error/fallback/invocation of expensive kernel sample full traces).

Span-level examples:
1) runtime.generate:init
   - start: when request accepted
   - attrs: model, route, request_id, batching_mode
2) kv.cache_lookup
   - start/end fast span
   - attrs: key_hit (true|false), shard, cache_ttl_ms, evicted_recently
3) kernel.execute
   - long-running; emits partial events for token slices
   - attrs: kernel_name, quant_mode, gpu_mem_mb, seq_processed
4) router.fanout
   - captures multi-model fanout decisions, attrs: strategies_tried (list), fallback_reason

Dashboard layout guidance (investigation-first):
- Top row (incident quick-assesment): total request count (1m/5m), first_token p95, token_tail p99, fallback rate (1m), kvcache.hit_ratio aggregated by route. Keep these as single-line sparklines for quick eyeballing.
- Middle row (attribution): latency heatmap by route x region (quantiles), distribution of kv_warmth across traffic, kernel time breakdown stacked by kernel_name.
- Bottom row (drill panels): example traces (rotating top N by severity), recent rollback/deployment markers, per-tenant outlier list.
- Panel hygiene: add a short blurb in panel description: "what to run next" (e.g., queries to reproduce, relevant runbook anchor).

Heatmap specifics:
- Use coherent quantile bands: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 columns; route rows sorted by active request rate. Color by p95 with tooltip for p99. Heatmap should default to last 10m with 1m resolution.

Alerting/prioritization rules (suggestions):
- Alert A (Severe): p99(first_token) > baseline * 3 AND fallback rate > 0.5% for > 5m -> Page oncall SRE.
- Alert B (Medium): per-route kvcache.hit_ratio drops > 20% relative to 1h baseline -> Slack alert to serving-runtime channel.
- Alert C (Low): trace.sampled_ratio_by_route dips below configured sampling_policy for 30m -> ticket for telemetry team.

Instrumentation rollout checklist (small, iterative):
- Step 0: pick 3 routes (high, mid, low traffic) as canaries.
- Step 1: add inference.latency.first_token_ms histogram + kvcache.hit_ratio gauge (low overhead).
- Step 2: instrument fallback.invocations_total and router.fanout span.
- Step 3: create dashboard with top row + heatmap and validate with synthetic probe.
- Step 4: enable limited trace sampling for canary routes; verify trace links show fallback attribute.
- Step 5: run a 2-week trial, collect feedback from SREs and serving engineers, prune panels that were unused.

Operational heuristics / quick tips:
- Avoid highly cardinal labels on high-frequency metrics (e.g., do not add user_id on counters). If needed, add low-cardinality cohort labels (customer_tier).
- Derive heavy-weight signals (costly aggregations) in an offline aggregator and expose as gauge to dashboards.
- Use synthetic probes per-region to keep a guaranteed slice of data for SLO checks.
- When adding a new span attribute, add a single-line note to the span docs and add a dashboard link. Small docs + examples matter.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide:
- Sampling policy: deterministic low-rate versus adaptive sampling (adaptive captures anomalies but harder to reason about costs). Recommend deterministic + error-burst overrides for now.
- Span size: how much token-level context to include? We should limit to index markers and rare debug-only toggles to avoid trace bloat.
- Alarm sensitivity: conservative initial thresholds, but build quick tuning runbook so product teams can adjust per-route thresholds.

Short-term todos (owner: Priya):
- [ ] Create PR for metric name documentation (README + examples) — due 2025-10-06 (ref: github:repo/telemetry#456)
- [ ] Wire top-row dashboard panels for the 3 canary routes — due 2025-10-09
- [ ] Add kvcache.hit_ratio telemetry for serving runtime (small exporter) — coordinate with Derek — due 2025-10-12
- [ ] Draft quick troubleshooting runbook (3-minute flow) and attach to dashboard descriptions — due 2025-10-16

Notes to self / context snippets:
- We discussed aligning 'kv_warmth' tag values across store implementations. Need a shared enum: hot,warm,cold,unknown.
- For tenant-sensitive metrics, ensure no PII in span attrs. Use tenant_tier not tenant_id in public dashboards.

References / anchors:
- Confluence page with SLOs: confluence:OBS-234-instrumentation-lens
- Jira epic: OBS-1283 (telemetry prioritization)
- Slack thread: #observability (search: "prio lens")

If anyone wants to pair on the canary routes selection, ping Liam or Sofia. This remains a draft — please add inline comments and sample queries that made investigations easier in the past.
